editorial.description_en: Moss growing where water runs over it, kept brighter than moss on land.
editorial.description_ja: 川の中の苔のような、しずんだ緑。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.712, C 0.048, h 146.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 川 (kawa, river) + 苔 (koke, moss), rendaku to -goke. It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "River Moss" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 川苔. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — ishi-midori at ΔE00 5.5, sugi-kage at ΔE00 5.8, waka-shida at ΔE00 7.9. complementary is empty because no entry in this corpus sits within 22° of the opposite hue. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
